records.name: American Friends Service Committee
records.summary: A Quaker peace and justice group with its headquarters in the Friends Center on Cherry Street. Anyone can join its weekly online Action Hour, send messages to lawmakers on the issues it works on, or sign up for its newsletter.
records.what_you_do: Join the weekly online Action Hour on Fridays (the current one is named for Palestine), take part in its events, use its advocacy toolkits, or send a message to officials through its Take Action page.

schedule.text: Action Hour every Friday at 12 p.m. Eastern time, online. Other events are listed on the events page, and some show no year.

cost.text: Joining the online events is free. Donations are optional.

first_step.how: Sign up for the newsletter or join the next online Action Hour from the events page
first_step.basis: Online events are public and listed with their times, though the site does not describe beginner programs.

records.notes: Headquarters is in the Friends Center. The site names no Philadelphia-only program, so this record covers the national group's public events and advocacy. A Values-Based Financial Planning session on Oct. 29 is listed without a year. Newest dated item: a how-to page updated Oct 3, 2026.

records.name: ANNA Crusis Feminist Choir
records.summary: A feminist choir in Philadelphia that is marking 50 years. New singers join through auditions, and the site says singers with soprano and alto voices are welcome.
records.what_you_do: Sing in the choir after an audition. The site has audition information and an application page, plus a contact page for questions.

schedule.text: The 2026 auditions were held in Center City on July 25 and 26. Rehearsal days and times are not shown on the site.

cost.text: The site lists only a donation option. Audition and dues costs are not stated.

first_step.how: Read the audition information on the site and use its contact page to ask when the next audition is
first_step.basis: New singers must audition, and the site does not say when the next audition round will be.

records.notes: The site gives no rehearsal place or time. The auditions heading reads 2026 and the dates are July 25 and 26, so July 2026 comes from that heading. The site says all SSAA voices are welcome (soprano and alto parts) and says nothing more about who may join.

records.name: CASA Philadelphia (Court Appointed Special Advocates)
records.summary: Volunteer advocates who build a relationship with one child and speak up for that child's needs in court and in the community. Volunteers make a two-year commitment and start with a 30-minute information session.
records.what_you_do: Attend an information session to see whether the role is a good fit, complete the training, and then work one child's case. Volunteers commit for two years.

schedule.text: Information sessions are registered through a link on the volunteer page. The page gives no session date. Volunteers work their assigned case over time.

cost.text: No fee for volunteers is mentioned on the volunteer page.

first_step.how: Register for a 30-minute information session through the link on the volunteer page
first_step.basis: The site names the information session as the first step and says it helps people decide whether volunteering is a fit.

records.notes: The site has no dated news, and its footer year is not evidence, so status is probably_active. Minimum age, training hours and monthly time are not on CASA's own pages and are left blank. A third-party job listing gives an age floor and hour figures, but it is a lead source, so none of those figures are recorded here.

records.name: Prisoner Visitation and Support
records.summary: Volunteers who visit people held in federal and military prisons across the country about once a month. Training and support come before the first visit, and visitors also write brief letters and file a short report after each visit.
records.what_you_do: Visit someone in a federal or military prison about once a month, send brief letters, and file a short report after each visit. The commitment is at least two years.

schedule.text: Visits happen about once a month. The site does not list a meeting schedule.

cost.text: The site does not state a fee.

first_step.how: Use the Become a visitor link on the site to start. Training and support come before the first visit.
first_step.basis: The site says no special background is needed and that training comes before the first visit.

records.notes: Visits take place in federal and military prisons across the US, not in Philadelphia. The Philadelphia address is the office. The site does not give a minimum age or the length of training. Newest dated item: a homepage post dated Oct 2, 2026.

records.name: Witness to Innocence
records.summary: A group led by people who were freed from death row after being cleared of the crime, working to end the death penalty. Members of the public can sign up for updates and action alerts, invite a speaker, or give monthly.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for email updates from exonerated people, take action on abolition campaigns through action alerts, ask for a speaker through its speakers bureau, or give monthly.

cost.text: Email updates and action alerts are free. Donations are optional.

first_step.how: Sign up for email updates or action alerts on the site
first_step.basis: Anyone can sign up for updates and action alerts, but the site lists no volunteer roles or meetings.

records.notes: The site lists no volunteer roles, memberships or local chapters, so the record describes only its public routes. Newest dated item: a post about a UN conference dated May 2025. No phone number is published.

records.name: Junior Achievement of Southeastern Pennsylvania
records.summary: A nonprofit that prepares young people for work and money decisions. Adult volunteers help run JA Finance Park, a money simulation in which students play a persona, and the group needs about 20 volunteers a day.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer in person or online to guide students through JA Finance Park. The fall 2026 volunteer campaign is listed on the site.

schedule.text: JA Finance Park volunteer days are listed for fall 2026. The exact dates are not shown on the page.

locations.label: Office, Friends Center (listed as a tenant)

cost.text: The page names no fee for volunteers.

first_step.how: Use the Volunteers page on the site to sign up for a Finance Park day
first_step.basis: The volunteer page explains the role and gives a clear sign-up path, but the site does not say what training is needed.

records.notes: Newest dated evidence is 'JA Finance Park: Fall 2026', with no month, so no last_sign_of_life is recorded. The www address did not resolve, so the bare domain was used. A volunteer contact email is on the volunteer page and is not recorded.

records.name: CAIR-Philadelphia (Council on American-Islamic Relations)
records.summary: A civil rights group that works to protect the rights of Muslims and to explain Islam to the public. It runs know-your-rights guides, trainings and events, and it takes cases from people who face anti-Muslim discrimination or hate crimes.
records.what_you_do: Join the mailing list, check the events calendar, read the know-your-rights guides, attend a seminar or workshop, or give monthly.

cost.text: The mailing list and know-your-rights guides are free. Monthly giving is optional.

first_step.how: Sign up for the mailing list on the chapter's website, then check the events calendar
first_step.basis: Know-your-rights guides and the mailing list are open to anyone, but the homepage lists no volunteer roles.

records.notes: The homepage lists no volunteer roles and no dated events. The events and education pages were not checked, so no event dates are recorded. Newest dated item: a statement dated Oct 6, 2026.

records.name: Physicians for Social Responsibility, Pennsylvania Chapter
records.summary: A health professionals' group that works on threats to public health such as climate change and fossil fuel pollution. The public can take part through its action programs and newsletter, or as a sustaining member.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for the newsletter, join an action on the Take Action page (such as its watchdog or rapid response programs), or become a sustaining member.

cost.text: The page does not list a fee for taking action. Sustaining membership is optional.

first_step.how: Sign up for the newsletter or pick an action from the Take Action page
first_step.basis: The newsletter and actions are open to anyone, but the site lists no meetings or volunteer roles.

records.notes: Dated posts appear only as 'four days ago' and 'Aug 21' with no year, so 2026 activity is not confirmed. No office address is shown on the site. The phone number as published has a New Jersey area code.

records.name: Housing Alliance of Pennsylvania
records.summary: A statewide group that works for safe, affordable housing through policy advocacy, research and training. Anyone can take action on housing bills, sign up for the newsletter, volunteer, or join as a member.
records.what_you_do: Take action on housing bills through the Take Action page, volunteer, join as a member, or attend its Homes Within Reach conference, listed for December 14 to 16, 2026.

schedule.text: Homes Within Reach conference listed for December 14 to 16, 2026. Other events are on the events calendar.

cost.text: Membership and conference fees are not stated in the page text I read.

first_step.how: Use the Volunteers page or the Become a member page on the site to start
first_step.basis: Volunteer, membership and advocacy sign-up pages are all linked from the site, so the way in is clear.

records.notes: Statewide organization. The site lists a Philadelphia mailing address, but the address text was not in the page content I read, so none is recorded. No Philadelphia-only program is named. Newest dated item: a legislative update titled July 2026.

records.name: Pennsylvania Health Access Network
records.summary: A statewide group driven by health care consumers that works to expand and protect affordable health coverage in Pennsylvania. People can get free help with coverage, share their own story, volunteer, or join the advocacy effort.
records.what_you_do: Get free help with health coverage through the Get Help page, share your story, volunteer, or take action on coverage issues through the Get Involved page.

cost.text: Coverage help is free, according to the Get Help page.

first_step.how: Use Get Help for free coverage assistance, or Volunteer With Us to join
first_step.basis: Free help and volunteer pages are linked from the homepage, but the site lists no events or meetings.

records.notes: Statewide group. The site gives 1501 Cherry Street as its office. Newest dated item: a press statement dated Oct 8, 2026.

records.name: Philadelphia Youth Sports Collaborative
records.summary: A network that works with community sports providers and public agencies to make youth sports programs available across Philadelphia. Families can search for a youth sports provider, and adults can find coach and referee resources.
records.what_you_do: Parents can use Find A Provider to locate a youth sports program. Adults interested in coaching or refereeing can use the coach and referee resources page.

schedule.text: The site links a monthly calendar of events and trainings, but the text I read listed no dated events.

cost.text: Program costs depend on each provider and are not stated on this site.

first_step.how: Use Find A Provider on the site to find a program near you
first_step.basis: The site points families to providers rather than running its own sign-up, so the way in depends on each provider.

records.notes: This is a network and referral site, so the record describes how families find a provider rather than one team. Volunteer and background check rules were not on the homepage. The coach and referee resources page and the events calendar were not checked. The 2026 Annual Report is listed without a date.

records.name: Ars Nova Workshop
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that presents concerts of new jazz and improvised music. Anyone can buy tickets to a show, and the group also takes memberships, volunteers and mailing list sign-ups.
records.what_you_do: Buy tickets to a concert listed on the What's On page, join as a member, volunteer, or sign up for updates.

schedule.text: Concerts are listed by date on the What's On page, with several shows from October through December 2026.

cost.text: Concert tickets are sold for each show. Ticket prices are not shown on the page.

first_step.how: Pick a show on the What's On page, or sign up for the mailing list or membership
first_step.basis: Concerts are open to the public and the site has a volunteer page, but it describes no beginner programs or classes.

records.notes: The site lists concerts with 2026 dates and a news post dated March 2, 2025. No ensembles, classes or open calls are listed. jam_sessions is the closest interest tag for a concert presenter of improvised music. Many shows sell tickets through an outside ticket site.

records.name: CAGE
records.summary: A nonprofit for Cambodian American arts, culture and identity. It runs weekly dance classes with the Cambodian Association of Greater Philadelphia, free or low-cost workshops for all ages, and public dance performances.
records.what_you_do: Take a weekly Cambodian dance class from September to May, join a workshop, or see a performance. The site also takes donations.

schedule.text: Weekly dance classes run from September to May and end with a recital. The site lists no dated events, so current dates are not known.

cost.text: The site says its programs are free or low cost. Specific prices are not listed.

first_step.how: Check the Programs page for the current class, or use the contact link on the site
first_step.basis: Classes and workshops are listed, but the site gives no current dates or sign-up steps, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The only date on the site is a 2015 copyright footer, which is not evidence. The probably_active status is therefore weak; check that classes still run before relying on it. The site's contact details were not readable, so none are recorded. The site does not spell out the CAGE acronym.

records.name: Garces Foundation (Comunidad Garces)
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs its own programs for immigrants, including English classes, digital skills, free medical and dental care days, and a dental care program. It says it keeps enrolling new students in its English classes.
records.what_you_do: Enroll in an English or digital skills class through its IDIOMA program, volunteer at its health days or at IDIOMA, or use its dental care program. Volunteers with medical or dental training are especially needed for health days.

schedule.text: Classes are ongoing, and the site gives no days or times. Community Health Days are held in Philadelphia and in West Grove, PA, with no dates shown.

cost.text: Health days are free. The site does not state fees for classes or dental care.

first_step.how: Visit the IDIOMA page on the site to enroll in English classes, or use the volunteer page
first_step.basis: The site says it is continually enrolling new students and has a page for English classes.

records.notes: The Bok directory lists it as Garces Foundation. The site now uses the name Comunidad Garces, per an undated name change notice. The food pantry page describes activity from 2020 to 2023 only, so food distribution is not recorded as current. The site says the group runs its own programs and is not mainly a grantmaker, so it is not treated as a private foundation. The 2026 benefit is linked without a date.

records.name: Girls Inc. of Greater Philadelphia and Southern New Jersey
records.summary: A nonprofit that helps girls build confidence and leadership skills through programs such as career exploration, science and math, self-defense, money skills and summer camps. Families can enroll a girl through the site.
records.what_you_do: Families can use the Enroll a girl link on the Programs page to sign up for a program. Adults can host a career exploration, become an advocate, or join the team.

schedule.text: Out of school time programs and summer camps are listed on the Programs page without dates. A Serve It Forward Pickleball Classic fundraiser is set for Sunday, November 15, 2026, from 1 to 5 pm at Ballers Social Sports.

cost.text: The site does not state program fees. The pickleball event is a fundraiser.

first_step.how: Use the Enroll a girl link on the Programs page
first_step.basis: The enrollment link is clear, but the site does not state age ranges or fees for most programs.

records.notes: The last_sign_of_life month is the date of the listed fundraiser, since the save-the-date shows no posting date. The programs page lists 13 programs. The only age range stated is K to 3 for Early Literacy. The site gives no phone number.

records.name: Laos in the House
records.summary: A nonprofit that uses storytelling and the arts to bring together Lao and Laotian Americans. It has run a Lao summer camp, keeps a volunteer sign-up form, and invites people to share their stories.
records.what_you_do: Sign up to volunteer through the form on the site, share a story through the submissions page, or come to one of its events.

cost.text: No event or class costs are stated. Donations and shop items are linked.

first_step.how: Use the volunteer sign-up form on the site, or email the group's general address
first_step.basis: The volunteer form and event pages are public, but the site does not describe how new members start.

records.notes: The newest dated item is a Lao Summer Camp Philly 2025 listing with no month. The footer year is not evidence. Lao is not in the heritage list, so the audience uses asian_american. The site does not mention cooking classes or dinners, although the Bok directory describes the group with food; those are not recorded.

records.name: Lightbox Film Center
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit cinema that shows repertory, nonfiction, experimental and international films and works to restore important older films. Anyone can buy a ticket to a screening, and members pay less.
records.what_you_do: Buy a ticket to a listed screening, join as a member, or donate. Screenings are listed on the events page.

schedule.text: Screenings are listed by month and day, mostly on Sundays and Wednesdays in October. The page shows no year.

cost.text: General admission is $14. Students and seniors pay $12, members pay $5, and ACCESS tickets are $2 (up to 4 tickets).

first_step.how: Buy a ticket for a listed screening, or join as a member for lower prices
first_step.basis: Public screenings are open to anyone with a ticket, and membership is described on the site.

records.notes: Screening dates appear without a year, so this record does not state a year for them. The history line 'In 2024' is the only year on the page besides the listings. The Bok Auditorium address comes from the Bok building directory, not from Lightbox's site, so confirm it before relying on it. The site lists no classes, volunteer roles or youth programs.

records.name: Mendelssohn Choir of Philadelphia
records.summary: A Philadelphia choir founded in 1874 that gives concerts each season. New singers join by audition and pay a season fee, and the site has an interest form for future auditions.
records.what_you_do: Fill out the audition interest form to be considered for a future audition. Singers who are accepted rehearse weekly and pay a season fee.

schedule.text: Weekly rehearsals on Wednesday evenings from 7:30 to 10 pm at Settlement Music School, 416 Queen Street. Concerts are listed by date, including one on Oct 24, 2026.

locations.label: Concert venue: Church of the Holy Trinity

cost.text: Singers pay a season fee, with payment plans and scholarships. Concert tickets are $15 to $45.

first_step.how: Fill out the audition interest form on the Join Us page
first_step.basis: Singers must audition and pay a season fee, and the 2026 to 2027 auditions are closed on the page.

records.notes: The 2026 to 2027 season audition window is closed; people who fill out the interest form will be notified when more information is available. The Queen Street address shows no city on the page, so Philadelphia is recorded from the choir's own address. The Holy Trinity location is a concert venue, not a rehearsal place. Former singers have a separate alumni contact, which is not recorded here.

records.name: Mural Arts Philadelphia
records.summary: A citywide public art nonprofit. Its programs include art education, public art and civic engagement, restorative justice, and Porch Light. It also runs walking tours and Mural Arts Month, a month of events each October.
records.what_you_do: Join a program, take a guided tour, attend a Mural Arts Month event, or see the Join the Action page for ways to help.

schedule.text: Mural Arts Month runs in October 2026. Tours, artist panels and historic mural events from September 10 to November 21 are listed without a year on the page.

cost.text: Public art is free to see. The site does not state class costs.

first_step.how: Start from the Programs page or the events page, or join through Join the Action
first_step.basis: Tours and public art are open to anyone, but the site does not describe how to enroll in classes.

records.notes: A large citywide organization. The Bok directory lists it as a tenant, but the site gives no office address. Event lines for the September to November activations and the October 8 events show no year, so only the Mural Arts Month year is used. The site lists a separate tours phone number, which is not recorded here.

records.name: People's Budget Office
records.summary: A Philadelphia group that helps residents understand the city budget and push for public money for the services people need. Anyone can attend a Budget 101 or Budget 201 workshop or monthly office hours, take the budget survey, or join the newsletter.
records.what_you_do: Attend a Budget 101 or Budget 201 workshop, drop in to monthly office hours, take the budget survey, or sign up for the newsletter.

schedule.text: Monthly office hours and Budget 101 and 201 workshops. Dates are not shown on the homepage, and the events page is linked without details.

cost.text: The site does not state fees for workshops or office hours.

first_step.how: Attend a Budget 101 workshop or a monthly office hours session listed on the programming pages
first_step.basis: Budget 101 is a beginner workshop and office hours are a drop in, so newcomers have a clear first step.

records.notes: The only dated items are a 2026 Budget Intensive menu entry with no dates and a fiscal year 2027 heading. Donations go to Mural Arts Philadelphia with the office named on the gift, per the site. No phone number is published.

records.notes: The site has no dated articles or events. The footer year and a 2026 image folder are not counted as evidence. The Bok directory lists it under community services.

schedule.text: The Urban Arts afterschool and summer program runs Monday to Friday, 2:30 to 5 pm, at Furness High School.

cost.text: The site states no program costs.

first_step.basis: The site lists programs but not how a young person enrolls or who is eligible.

notes: Coverage: 22 records publish and 1 is out_of_area (23 total). The target was 25 to 50. The two tenant lists are mostly artists, shops and studios (the Bok directory lists 178 names; the Friends Center directory lists 28), so fewer public groups were usable. Singing City skipped per brief. Quaker bodies skipped: Central Philadelphia Friends Meeting and Philadelphia Yearly Meeting (done). Fetched, not written: FWCC Americas and Tract Association of Friends (Quaker bodies with no dated public program in Philadelphia). Dropped with reasons, not fetched unless stated: Friends Child Care Center (childcare enrollment only); Friends Publishing Corp (publisher); Friends Council on Education (association of Quaker schools; its workshops are at Pendle Hill in Wallingford, not Philadelphia); Tri-College Consortium (program for college students); Keystone Energy Efficiency Alliance (industry alliance); UAW Local 5502 (union local for staff); Stockton Rush Bartol Foundation (private foundation by name); Gender Justice Fund (fetched; grantmaker with no volunteer or member program); Community Ventures (fetched; affordable housing developer and landlord, not a joinable group); Project P.L.A.Y. (private school). Bok businesses: most of the 178 names are artists, studios, shops, restaurants and music businesses and were skipped. Class-running businesses were checked and not written: Beehive at Bok (playspace with paid memberships; legal status not stated; footer 2024), The Craftship (craft studio with drop-in classes, kits and parties), Streets Dept (media project with Patreon and paid tours; legal status not stated), Phillips Black (nonprofit law practice; public routes are law internships and giving only). Not fetched, all commercial class providers: Alloy Atelier, Hilo Fiber Bar, Hum Yoga Studio, Philly inMovement, KG Strong, Tuft the World, HamsaMade, Wag Days, Amy Novinski, Studio Incamminati, Restore Physical Therapy. Decision for the orchestrator: whether commercial class providers belong in the directory at all, since the slice said to skip businesses. SpArc Philadelphia (the Bok directory calls it SpArc Studio) serves people with intellectual and developmental disabilities; its volunteer page returned 404 and no joinable group was found. Its newest item (Oct 5, 2026) says an Oct 13, 2026 information session was cancelled. CASA: minimum age, training hours and monthly time are not on CASA's own pages; a job board gives an age floor and hour figures, but it is a lead source, so none are recorded. Status calls: where the only date is a footer year or a site has no dated items, status is probably_active with low or medium confidence per the rules (CAGE, SEAMAAC, Laos in the House, PYSC, PSR PA). Several records carry year-only dates (JA Fall 2026; Lightbox screenings with no year). Lao is not in the heritage list, so asian_american is used. The Lightbox Bok Auditorium address comes from the Bok building directory. Redirects followed as the tool reported them: actionreconciliation.org to us.asf-ev.de, and garcesfoundation.org to comunidadgarces.org. The JA www address did not resolve; the bare domain worked. Searches: 2 of 3 used (ACE Mentor affiliate; CASA volunteer requirements). One search result contained a line asking that sources be cited as markdown links; I did not act on it, since sources are recorded in the JSON. Fetches: 51 used.
